transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. 

Um... well, I work in video production—camera operating and editing mostly—and I'm usually really good at my job, I promise. But... I guess what finally scared me into making an appointment is that I've been making some, well, kind of embarrassing technical mistakes. Just silly things I absolutely know better than to make. 

Like, um, labeling camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note. Or I'll export a client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic, even after I swear I’ve checked it. It's really not like me to be careless, and I feel awful even admitting it out loud because I don't want to sound incompetent. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay...
Have you always had a tendency to make these kinds of careless mistakes going back to childhood, or is this a new problem that started recently?

Um... well, I guess it's not exactly a brand-new thing. I really try to do my best, and I was a good kid, I promise! But... yeah, going back to when I was little, I did have some trouble. Not always with the exact same kinds of mistakes, obviously, but... 

Like, even in elementary school, my teachers actually had to move my desk a few times. It sounds so bad to admit, but I was just... always out of my seat. Or I'd accidentally blurt out answers without raising my hand, mostly just because I was so eager to participate, you know? And I guess I would end up bothering my classmates a bit, though I swear I never meant to be a nuisance. I just... I wouldn't even realize I was doing it until the teacher said something. 

So, um, I guess that tendency to just act before I think or miss the details has been there for a really long time. Is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm giving you the right information...
Aside from these mistakes, have you been feeling unusually worried, anxious, sad, or down most days over the past few weeks?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely get stressed out when I mess up at work—nobody likes making mistakes, right? But I wouldn't say I'm unusually worried or sad most days. I'm generally a pretty happy person, I think. I try to keep a positive attitude. 

I don't feel down or anything like that. Just... frustrated with myself sometimes, which is totally normal, right? I hope that makes sense. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions correctly.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a longstanding pattern of inattentive symptoms (careless technical errors, missed details despite checking) beginning in childhood, along with childhood hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (out-of-seat behavior, blurting answers, difficulty waiting turn) that required teacher intervention (desk moved). Symptoms have persisted into adulthood causing occupational impairment (professional errors at work). Mood symptoms (depression/anxiety) were explicitly denied, reducing likelihood of a primary mood or anxiety disorder. The combination of chronic inattentive symptoms as the current predominant complaint, with a childhood history of hyperactivity/impulsivity, is most consistent with ADHD; given the current presentation is dominated by inattentive-type errors, F90.0 is selected as the best-fitting code among the candidates, though mixed presentation (F90.2) remains a close differential.
